brief.t: A large private bank with 6,275 branches and extension counters and 12,796 ATMs (March 2026).
Led by MD & CEO Amitabh Chaudhry since January 2019; his current term runs to 31 December 2027.
FY 2025-26 net profit was ₹24,457 crore, down 7%, mainly because the bank set aside more money for possible bad loans.
Q2 FY27 (Jul–Sep 2026) profit jumped 37.6% to ₹7,003 crore as provisions fell; Gross NPA improved to 1.16%.
Its net interest margin slipped to 3.36% in Q2 FY27, lower than most large rivals.

timeline.t: Started as UTI Bank, promoted by Unit Trust of India and other financial institutions.
Amitabh Chaudhry, earlier CEO of HDFC Life, became MD & CEO.
Took over Citibank's consumer business in India.
Former RBI Deputy Governor N S Vishwanathan became Part-time Chairman.
Vishwanathan began a new three-year term as Chairman, approved by RBI.

model.how: Axis earns mainly from the gap between the interest it charges on loans and the interest it pays depositors, plus fees from cards, payments, loans and group companies in mutual funds, broking and finance.
flow: Bank lends to people and businesses

points: RBI must approve a private bank's CEO and Chairman. That's why Axis's Chairman needed RBI clearance for his 2026 term.
Axis competes with HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank for salaried customers, cards and business loans.
Big theme for interviews: banks are opening branches while using AI to keep headcount flat.

people.name: Amitabh Chaudhry
people.note: Earlier MD & CEO of HDFC Life for over nine years. Engineer from BITS Pilani and MBA from IIM Ahmedabad. Current term runs to Dec 2027.

people.name: N S Vishwanathan

numbers.say: Axis Bank's profit rose 38% last quarter mainly because it needed to set aside much less for bad loans, while its margin is still under pressure.

rivals.note: Axis Bank is third among private banks by profit, after HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank.

network.local: Axis Bank added about 400 branches in FY26 while its staff fell, so new branches are run with smaller, more sales-focused teams.

employer.note: Headcount fell even as branches grew, a sign of more automation. Axis says an AI assistant now helps its branch staff answer queries.

csr.t: Axis Bank's CSR work is run mainly through the Axis Bank Foundation, focused on rural livelihoods and skills.

glossary.Net profit: What is left after all costs, provisions and taxes. The bank's final earnings.
glossary.Net Interest Income: Interest earned on loans minus interest paid on deposits. A bank's main earning.
glossary.Net interest margin: Net Interest Income as a % of the bank's interest-earning assets. Shows how profitable lending is.
glossary.Gross NPA: Non-Performing Asset: a loan not repaid for 90+ days. Gross NPA is the % of all loans that have gone bad.
glossary.Net NPA: Bad loans after subtracting the money already set aside (provisions) for them. Lower is better.
glossary.CASA ratio: Share of deposits in Current and Savings accounts. These pay little interest, so a higher CASA means cheaper funds.
glossary.Capital adequacy ratio: The bank's own capital compared with the risk in its loans. RBI requires a minimum; higher means safer.
glossary.Provisions: Money set aside from profit to cover loans that may not be repaid.
glossary.Deposits: Money customers keep with the bank in savings, current and fixed deposit accounts.
glossary.Advances: Loans given by the bank to customers and businesses.
glossary.Dividend: Part of the profit paid to shareholders, per share.
glossary.Treasury gains: Profit from buying and selling bonds and other investments. It can swing a lot each quarter.
glossary.Attrition: The % of employees who leave in a year. Also called employee turnover.
glossary.RBI: Reserve Bank of India, which regulates all banks in India.
glossary.KYC: Know Your Customer: checking a customer's identity before opening an account.
glossary.MSME: Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises: small businesses that banks lend to.
glossary.Cross-sell: Selling an extra product (like a credit card) to an existing customer.
glossary.Public sector bank: A bank where the Government of India owns the majority of shares.
glossary.BRSR: Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report: an official yearly report on people, environment and governance that big listed companies must publish.

Role knowledge, the bank and HR questions

Finance.q: Why did Axis Bank's profit rise 38% while operating profit grew only about 6%?
Finance.a: Because provisions (money set aside for bad loans) fell sharply. Lower credit costs, not just core income, drove the jump.
The bank made higher provisions, including a one-time buffer for standard assets in Q4, which reduced profit.

Finance.q: What is net interest margin, and what is Axis's?
Finance.a: The gap between interest earned and paid, as a % of assets. Axis's was 3.36% in Q2 FY27.

Marketing.q: How would you market Axis credit cards to first-time earners?
Marketing.a: Simple digital onboarding, rewards linked to UPI and online shopping, and clear messages on responsible use.

Marketing.q: Axis added about 400 branches. How would you launch one in a small town?
Marketing.a: Local events, current accounts for shopkeepers, salary accounts with nearby employers, and local-language messaging.

HR.q: Axis's headcount fell while branches grew. How would you keep employees engaged?
HR.a: Reskilling for digital and sales roles, internal moves, clear career paths and fair workload.

HR.q: How would you reduce attrition among new branch staff?
HR.a: Better onboarding, buddy mentors, realistic targets and early recognition.

Sales.q: Sell me an Axis Bank salary account.
Sales.a: Ask about needs first, then link zero-balance, app, card offers and insurance to them. Close with a next step.

Operations.q: How can AI help branch operations?
Operations.a: Answering staff queries quickly, faster KYC checks and fewer manual errors. Axis already uses an AI assistant for branch queries.

Other.q: What do you know about Axis Bank?
Other.a: India's third-largest private bank: ₹24,457 cr profit in FY26, 6,275 branches, led by Amitabh Chaudhry.
